tasks.title: Telescope
tasks.statement:
On the observational round you will use a simple Newton-system telescope with the mirror diameter O = 125 mm, focal length F = 1025 mm and 3 eye-pieces with focal lengths f1 = 12 mm, f2 = 25 mm and f3 = 38 mm. Find on what distances (Ax1 =, Ax2 =, Ax3 = in vertical direction on the middle figure) it is necessary to move the corresponding eye-pieces (1,2,3) to readjust the telescope from observation of the sky objects to observation of a monkey sitting at a distance L = 50 m from you. (Your answer should have both formula and numerical values.) What eyepiece is the most suitable for observation of the monkey? Why?

Addition for B group.

1+B. Telescope. L = 50 m as before, but now the monkey is running directly towards you (to steal something to eat) with a speed v = 3 m/s. Find the rate (in mm/s) of moving the most suitable eye-piece for readjusting the telescope to keep the monkey in focus.

parts.question: Find on what distances Ax1, Ax2, Ax3 it is necessary to move the corresponding eye-pieces to readjust the telescope from observation of the sky objects to observation of a monkey sitting at a distance L = 50 m, and determine the most suitable eyepiece with justification. For group B: find the rate of moving the most suitable eye-piece.

tasks.title: False star
tasks.statement:
The White Bear (whom was already met in the VII, VIII, IX and X International Astronomy Olympiads) decided to connect a telescope to a film photo camera to make photos of constellations. The exposure times used were of order of 5 minutes. His comrade Penguin appears to be a great joker and bought a photoflash lamp. He decided to play a trick on the Bear and to “put” an extra star in his sky image, while the Bear photographed near-horizon constellations. The Penguin sitting in the photographic area of the Bear’s telescope (of course, relatively far from the telescope — 2.5 km) flashed once (sent one light pulse) to the camera during the exposure. Estimate the stellar magnitude of the false star in the Bear’s image.

Take into account the parameters of the flash pulse. The photographic conditions (sensitivity of film, diaphragm) while photographing objects with the flash at the distance of 1.5 metres (from both flash and camera) should be the same as while photographing the same objects on a sunny day with an exposure time of about 1/1000 second.

The solution has to include a picture with images of the telescope, Bear and Penguin.

parts.question: Estimate the stellar magnitude of the false star in the Bear's image, including a picture with images of the telescope, Bear and Penguin.

tasks.title: Polar day and night
tasks.statement: Find the boundaries of the region of the polar day and the region of polar night at the dates when the Sun may be in Zenith in Mumbai, HBCSE. The latitude and longitude of HBCSE are Ac = 72° 56', фс = 19° 03'. Take as many effects as possible into account.

parts.question: Find the boundaries of the region of the polar day and the region of polar night at the dates when the Sun may be in Zenith in Mumbai, HBCSE.

tasks.title: Galaxy
tasks.statement:
Figure 4.1. shows the distribution of hydrogen gas in the disk of the spiral galaxy NGC 1325 as a contour map. The contour image is superimposed on an optical image of the galaxy. Assume the disk of the galaxy to be nearly circular. Find the angular diameter of the galaxy. (As the angular size of the galaxy is small to an observer on the Earth, you can use plane geometry as an approximation.) Estimate the diameter and distance to the galaxy in kpc. Find the angle of inclination of the galaxy plane with respect to the plane of the sky.

Addition for B group.

4+B. Galaxy. Figure 4.2. shows 2° in diameter region of sky near NGC 1325. A radiomessage on the wavelength λ = 20 cm has been sent to this region from the Earth in hope that after 260 years the sapiens habitants of system of star π Eri receive it. But the signal passed further and has been registered only by habitants of NGC 1325. Scientists of NGC 1325 also think that intelligence exists in π Eri system. What size of radiotelescope should be possessed by citizens of NGC 1325 to identify that the signal issued in Solar system but not in π Eri system.

parts.question: Find the angular diameter of the galaxy, estimate the diameter and distance to the galaxy in kpc, find the angle of inclination of the galaxy plane. For group B: find the required size of the radiotelescope for citizens of NGC 1325.

tasks.title: Lunar satellite
tasks.statement: These are two photos of the Moon taken by the same camera mounted on a lunar satellite. The first photo has been made while the satellite was near its periselenion and the second one near the aposelenion.

parts.question: For group A only: Find from these data the value of the satellite's orbit eccentricity. Estimate the minimum period between the moments at which these two photos could be taken. For group B only: Estimate the maximum possible period of orbit around the Moon of this satellite, considering the lunar orbit around Earth as circular.
